title: At Ahmedabad's Narendra Modi Stadium, Diljit Dosanjh Calls Out 'Double Standards' Over Concert Complaints
excerpt: The Punjabi star used his Aura World Tour stop at the world's largest cricket stadium to ask why Coldplay's lyrics draw no objections while his shows face repeated complaints — and answered his critics with two words.
body:
• Diljit Dosanjh performed at Ahmedabad's Narendra Modi Stadium on Saturday, November 21, as part of his Aura World Tour — a Punjabi-language set at the world's largest cricket stadium.
  • On stage, he called out what he described as double standards: complaints target his concerts, he said, while Coldplay songs referencing being "drunk and high" draw no objections.
  • He told the crowd he had watched Coldplay at the same stadium and dreamed of playing it himself; his message to those who file complaints against his shows was "Love You."
  • The Ahmedabad date was announced from the stage at London's Wembley Stadium in September, where Dosanjh headlined on the same tour.

Diljit Dosanjh used the biggest stage in Indian cricket to make a point about the scrutiny his concerts attract. Performing at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad on Saturday, the Punjabi singer and actor addressed what he described as double standards surrounding complaints against his performances, according to Aaj Tak and Punjabi Mania.

Dosanjh reportedly drew a comparison with Coldplay, the British band that has also played the stadium, questioning why their songs featuring references to being "drunk and high" do not attract the same objections that are repeatedly raised against his concerts. Complaints and restrictions have followed several of his live performances in India, and his remarks were read by fans as a direct response to that criticism.

A dream stated on the same ground

The venue itself was part of the message. Dosanjh recalled watching Coldplay perform at the Narendra Modi Stadium and said the experience inspired him to dream of performing at the same venue one day — an ambition Saturday's show fulfilled, as he brought his Aura World Tour to the stadium he had once watched from the audience. To the people who file complaints against his shows or try to create obstacles, his closing message was brief: "Love You."

How the Ahmedabad show was set up

The concert had been telegraphed for two months. Dosanjh announced the Ahmedabad date from the stage at London's Wembley Stadium on September 12, during the same Aura World Tour, telling the Wembley crowd that the biggest stadium is in India and that a Punjabi artist had to perform there; coverage of that announcement noted Coldplay's sold-out shows at the venue and Dosanjh's own congratulations to the band. The Ahmedabad performance also marked his return to the city after his 2024 Dil-Luminati India Tour.

For diaspora audiences who have followed the tour through Wembley and the European dates, Saturday's show closed a loop the singer himself had drawn: the complaint he answered in Ahmedabad was about Indian concerts, but the standard he measured himself against — a sold-out Narendra Modi Stadium — is one he first invoked in front of a London crowd. His set in Ahmedabad was in Punjabi, the language of the catalogue that has carried him from Punjab to the world's largest stages.
nri_angle: Dosanjh's stadium run links Wembley's diaspora crowd to a home-turf milestone, and his remarks speak to debates Punjabi audiences follow on both sides.
